hallucination_scrub_v0_1_60.why: lifted from license clause 'USE OR IMPLEMENTATION OF SUCH ARM TECHNOLOGY WILL NOT INFRINGE ...'; not a real product name

base_address: Defined at SoC level; offsets given relative to module base.
notes: If a future system-integration L4 is required, the canonical 'address-side fields' to capture would be: HADDR width (10..64), HBURST 1KB-boundary rule, HPROT[3:0]/HPROT[6:0] depending on Extended_Memory_Types property, HSEL signal per AHB Subordinate; PADDR width (up to 32), PPROT[2:0] (APB4), PSELx per peripheral.
rationale: AHB and APB are bus / interconnect protocols, not peripherals with a control register file. There is no MMIO register map in these documents. AHB carries the integrator-defined slave address on HADDR; APB carries it on PADDR. Concrete AHB/APB peripheral IP blocks define their own register file at the SoC integration level — outside these protocol specs.

AHB_HADDR_width_bits.note: In Issues A and B the address width was fixed at 32. Recommended range in Issue C is 10..64.

APB_PADDR_width_bits.note: Can be up to 32 bits wide; driven by the bridge.

address_side_field_widths.APB_minimum_subordinate_decode_granulari: Implementation-defined; one PSELx per peripheral slot.
